observed: Polyth was SIGKILLed mid-turn while the owned OpenCode child and its active bash tool stayed alive. The child survived the crash. On restart, first runtime acquisition reaped the recorded child via the PID-record identity contract and spawned one fresh generation; no duplicate prompt (prompt_async POST count stayed 1 across both server lives), one tool side effect, one durable user intent, sqlite integrity ok. FAILURE: the session is permanently unusable after the restart. Its persisted runtime binding pins the previous boot's authorityId, but the owned lease mints `owned:${randomUUID()}` on every boot (createOpenCodeRuntime passes no stable authorityId), so the first-wire interaction (abort) failed 500 `binding-mismatch` ("persisted backend binding does not match the current endpoint") and the projection stayed stale `working` forever (>90s watch plus post-touch watch) with no live upstream turn and no recovery path.
expected: existing process/session handled per ownership contract; no duplicate prompt; active state survives

identifiers.rootCause: per-boot random owned authorityId invalidates every persisted session binding across Polyth restarts

escalation: ownership/state-machine issue escalated without patching: a stable-authority one-liner would also need cross-restart generation semantics (the generation counter is per-process too), so equal counter values could silently satisfy the generation-crossing check without proof
